Durable Milliner tickets. A lost response is not permission to submit again.
Notes: the owner's comments on anything Runesmith shows, and how they reach the model.

Confined organ process (runs as ``python -I -B organ_child.py``).
Operating-system limits for organ processes: a second barrier under the audit hook.
Pacing for free keys: when a service says it is at its limit, remember until when.
Judge-accepted fixes as reviewable patches: Runesmith proposes, a human decides.
A human-readable dashboard of one Runesmith home (REPORT.md).
Host side of confined organ execution.

Sharing generations between Runesmith homes: Kaizen that compounds across people.

library.name: C7
library.title: Reads what the failure says
library.summary: Before it asks a model where to look, C7 ranks your files by what the failure itself names: the files the failing tests executed, test names that match module names, and the class names in the error text. It then makes sure the top files are actually read. (A fourth step, module paths in the error text, only recognises its two development repositories' package names and does not fire on yours.)
library.evidence: SR7, a preregistered and sealed study (2026-09-25): on 54 unseen tasks in two Python repositories, C7 repaired 57 of 162 attempts (54 tasks, 3 rounds each) against its predecessor B's 35 of 162 with the same small model (p = 0.00085), with no more errors or false fixes and about half the time per successful repair.
library.caveat: C7 was proven against B, not against the shipped g0, on synthetic single-line bugs with one model (gpt-oss-20b). Which of its steps carried the gain was not tested. On your work it must win an online trial before it becomes active.
library.authored_by: Runesmith's Kaizen loop, with Claude Opus 4.5 as the author instrument
